reasoning: Recent polling over the last several weeks shows Democrat Roy Cooper consistently ahead of Republican Michael Whatley by mid–single to low–double digits in North Carolina’s 2026 U.S. Senate race, implying a current environment of roughly D+8–10 in that contest despite the state’s slight Republican lean structurally.[1][2][3][5][6][9][10] There are no fresh, head‑to‑head general‑election presidential polls of North Carolina within the last 45 days in the results gathered; available July polls focus on Trump approval rather than a named opponent, so I cannot credibly assign a numeric presidential margin from those data alone.[11][14] Taken together, the best current quantified view is that the **Senate race is D+8–10**, while the **presidential race margin is indeterminate** based on the last 45 days’ publicly reported, state‑specific polling located here.

sources.name: Fox News Poll (Beacon Research/Shaw & Co.)
sources.details: Fox News/Beacon Research/Shaw Company poll of 1,005 registered voters finds Roy Cooper 53% and Michael Whatley 44% in the North Carolina U.S. Senate race, a Cooper lead of 9 points.

sources.name: The Hill summary of Fox News poll
sources.details: News write‑up of the Fox News poll reports Cooper preferred by 53% of voters to 44% for Whatley in the race to replace Sen. Thom Tillis, a 9‑point Democratic lead.

sources.name: Elon University Poll
sources.details: Elon University Poll of 800 North Carolina adults (466 likely voters) finds among likely voters Cooper 53% and Whatley 42% in the U.S. Senate race, an 11‑point Democratic lead.

sources.name: The Hill on Elon University Poll
sources.details: News article summarizing the Elon University Poll reports Cooper at 53% and Whatley at 42% among likely voters in the North Carolina Senate race, describing Cooper as leading by double digits.

sources.name: Pressure of Truth write‑up of Elon Poll
sources.details: Secondary piece describes the Elon University survey, noting Cooper at 53% and Whatley at 42% among likely voters, and characterizes the race as one where Cooper continues to lead.

sources.name: Roll Call summarizing PPP poll
sources.details: Roll Call article cites a Public Policy Polling survey showing Cooper at 48% and Whatley at 44% in the North Carolina Senate race, a 4‑point Democratic edge earlier in July.

sources.name: AOL compilation of multiple NC Senate polls
sources.details: Roundup article reports several recent polls: Elon (53–42 Cooper), Carolina Journal (51.5–39 Cooper), Carolina Forward (49–42 Cooper), Change Research (50–41 Cooper), and Fox News (53–44 Cooper), all showing Cooper ahead by mid‑single to low‑double digits.
sources.date_range: July 29-August 1, 2026 (plus multiple late‑July and early‑August dates)

sources.name: Daily Kos elections write‑up of Fox News poll
sources.details: Daily Kos elections piece discusses the Fox News North Carolina Senate poll showing Cooper at 53% and Whatley at 44%, emphasizing that Trump’s preferred candidate is significantly trailing his Democratic rival.

sources.name: Change Research poll (reported via AOL)
sources.details: Article summarizing a Change Research poll notes Cooper leading Whatley 50% to 41% among North Carolina voters in the Senate race, a 9‑point Democratic advantage.

sources.name: Carolina Journal poll (reported via AOL)
sources.details: Carolina Journal poll of 600 likely voters, as summarized in a news article, shows Cooper leading Whatley 51.5% to 39%, a 12.5‑point Democratic margin in the North Carolina Senate race.

sources.name: Carolina Forward poll (reported via AOL)
sources.details: Carolina Forward sampling, as reported in an article, finds Cooper leading Whatley 49% to 42% in the Senate race, a 7‑point margin for Democrats.

sources.name: Catawba College approval survey (reported in Citizen Times)
sources.details: Catawba College study is described as collecting approval ratings for the Senate candidates, with Cooper’s approval at 48% and Whatley’s at 34%, suggesting a more favorable environment for the Democrat but without a direct head‑to‑head ballot test.

sources.name: High Point University poll on Trump approval in North Carolina
sources.details: High Point University release reports that 38% of North Carolinians approve and 50% disapprove of Donald Trump’s job performance, but does not present a specific head‑to‑head presidential ballot test for this cycle.

sources.name: Charlotte Observer summary of Elon poll on Trump approval
sources.details: Charlotte Observer article notes an Elon poll where 54% of respondents disapprove of Trump, indicating an unfavorable climate for him in North Carolina but without naming a general election opponent.

sources.name: Cook Partisan Voting Index – North Carolina statewide
sources.details: Cook Partisan Voting Index table lists North Carolina as R+1, indicating the state voted one point more Republican than the nation as a whole in recent presidential elections.
